#Marks Data set 
```{r}
marks <- data.frame(
  Mathematics = c(70, 80, 90, 60),
  Economics = c(75, 85, 80, 65),
  Statistics = c(60, 70, 95, 75),
  Programming = c(70,90,55,88),
  Accounting = c(65, 75, 90, 77)
)
print(marks)
```
#Apply: apply() performs a function across the rows or columns of a matrix or array.
#mean on column
```{r}
apply(marks,2,mean)
```
#mean on rows
```{r}
apply(marks,1,mean)
```
#Columns summation
```{r}
apply(marks,2,sum)
```
#Rows Summation
```{r}
apply(marks,1,sum)
```
#lappy: lapply() applies a function to each element of a list or vector and always returns a list.
##lapply(X, FUN)
#Example
```{r}
marks <- list(
  Mathematics = c(70, 80, 90),
  Economics = c(75, 85, 80),
  Statistics = c(60, 70, 95)
)

lapply(marks, mean)
```
#Summation
```{r}
lapply(marks,sum)
```
#sapply: sapply() works similarly to lapply(), but it tries to simplify the result into a vector or matrix when possible
## sapply syntax: sapply(X, FUN)
sapply(marks,mean)
